text.text: Run the gym from one page. Members, their plans and their payments are linked, and every class or training session is a Booking. The Plans table shows churn and recurring value; Members shows who needs a call about a failed payment. Start on the Dashboard each morning.
Plans and pricing
What you sell, what it costs and how many members are on each plan.
Members
Everyone who has joined or enquired, with their plan, attendance and billing.
Bookings
Classes, training sessions and tours on the calendar, with attendance.
Payments
Charges, failed cards and refunds, tied to each client.
Bookings, payments and plan health at a glance.
Not yet marked
My bookings
Failed payments
Handle freezes cleanly and cancellations kindly. Most people who freeze come back.
Freezing a membership
Ask the member for the reason and the return date.
Set their status to Frozen and write the date in their notes.
Pause billing on the date they choose and note it on the next payment.
Set a reminder to message them a week before they return.
Cancelling
Offer a freeze or a cheaper plan first, once, without pressure.
Confirm the notice period and the last billing date.
Set the status to Cancelled and ask one question: what would have kept you?
A failed card is usually a new card, not a lost member. Call within two days.
Steps
Open Members and look for Fix payment in the Retention check column.
Call or text and ask them to update the card.
If it is fixed, mark the payment Paid.
After the second failure, pause class booking until it is resolved.
Tone
Always assume it was an expired card. Never say the word overdue on the first call.
Full classes keep the room feeling alive. Empty ones teach you what to move.
Every week
Review attendance for each class on the Bookings board.
Move or retire a class that averages under five people for a month.
Send trainers their schedule on Friday.
Trial offers
Book an orientation for every new member in their first week. Members who attend within seven days stay far longer.
